title: Network pharmacology integrated with multi-omics demonstrates that Wumei Wan modulates the progression of colorectal cancer by regulating the focal adhesion-YAP signaling axis.
authors: Yang, Shusen; Wang, Min; Liu, Siyue; Zhang, Yilin; Liu, Yushan; Yang, Mingjie; Wang, Wenba; Wang, Pengli; Zou, Junbo; Li, Jingtao; Yan, Shuguang; Si, Mingming; Wei, Hailiang
one_liner_zh: 该文通过网络药理学和多组学研究乌梅丸调节结直肠癌中黏着斑-YAP信号轴，虽含分子对接和MD模拟，但核心对象非蛋白质-DNA互作，且未涉及TF-DNA结合建模，仅边缘相关。
abstract: ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: Colorectal cancer(CRC) is one of the most common malignant tumors of the digestive system, and Traditional Chinese Medicine has shown good efficacy in its treatment and prognosis. Wumei Wan(WMW) is widely used in the treatment of digestive system and tumor diseases, with effects such as anti-diarrheal, anti-dysentery, and pain relief. Modern pharmacological studies suggest that its active ingredients have anti-inflammatory, antioxidant, and anti-tumor properties. However, there is still a lack of systematic research on the role of WMW in the prevention and treatment of CRC and its molecular mechanisms. AIM OF THIS STUDY: The aim of this study is to clarify the key active components and primary mechanisms by which WMW inhibits the initiation and progression of CRC, utilizing a multi-faceted approach including chemical composition analysis, network pharmacology, multi-omics studies, molecular biology validation, and molecular simulations. METHODS: UHPLC-HRMS/MS was used to identify the chemical components in WMW decoction and post-administration serum, and network pharmacology analysis was combined to predict potential targets and signaling pathways. Key differential pathways were selected through combined transcriptomics and proteomics analysis, and the expression patterns of the FAK/Src/YAP axis in CRC were verified using the GEO database. An azoxymethane/dextran sulfate sodium (AOM/DSS)-induced CRC mouse model was constructed to assess the effects of WMW on survival rate, tumor burden, histological changes in the colon, and the expression of related proteins. The expression of downstream genes CTGF and Axin2 was detected via qRT-PCR, and the regulatory effects of WMW-containing serum on FAK/Src/YAP signaling were examined in the HCT116 cells model. Finally, molecular docking and molecular dynamics simulations were performed. RESULTS: UHPLC-HRMS/MS analysis identified 15 circulating components of WMW following administration. Network pharmacology analysis revealed 241 overlapping targets between WMW-related targets and CRC-associated genes, which were enriched in pathways related to inflammation regulation, cell proliferation, and focal adhesions, with FAK/Src/YAP-related signaling features emerging as a central network module. In the AOM/DSS-induced CRC model, WMW treatment was associated with changes in body weight, tumor burden, and colonic mucosal structure, along with reduced tissue expression levels of VEGF and p53. Multi-omics analyses showed coordinated alterations in pathways related to inflammation, proliferation, and extracellular matrix (ECM) remodeling following WMW intervention. Analysis of GEO datasets confirmed elevated expression of PTK2, Src, and YAP1 in CRC tissues, supporting aberrant focal adhesion-YAP-associated signaling features in clinical CRC. In vivo and in vitro experiments showed that WMW intervention was associated with reduced phosphorylation levels of FAK, Src, and YAP, decreased stress fiber formation, attenuated YAP nuclear localization, and lower expression of CTGF and PCNA. Molecular docking and molecular dynamics simulations indicated that several circulating components could stably interact with the FAK kinase domain, with auraptene exhibiting relatively favorable binding characteristics. CONCLUSION: These findings suggest that WMW intervention is associated with coordinated alterations in inflammation-related signaling, cell proliferation, and extracellular matrix remodeling in CRC, with focal adhesion-YAP-related mechanotransduction representing a potential associated feature. This study provides integrated experimental evidence supporting further investigation of WMW and traditional Chinese medicine-based strategies targeting focal adhesion-associated signaling in CRC research.
abstract_zh: 民族药理学相关性：结直肠癌（CRC）是消化系统最常见的恶性肿瘤之一，中药在其治疗和预后中显示出良好疗效。乌梅丸（WMW）广泛用于消化系统及肿瘤疾病的治疗，具有止泻、抗痢疾和镇痛等作用。现代药理学研究表明，其活性成分具有抗炎、抗氧化和抗肿瘤特性。然而，关于WMW在CRC预防和治疗中的作用及其分子机制，仍缺乏系统性研究。本研究目的：本研究旨在利用化学成分分析、网络药理学、多组学研究、分子生物学验证和分子模拟等多方面方法，阐明WMW抑制CRC发生和进展的关键活性成分及主要机制。方法：采用UHPLC-HRMS/MS鉴定WMW煎剂及给药后血清中的化学成分，并结合网络药理学分析预测潜在靶点和信号通路。通过转录组学和蛋白质组学联合分析筛选关键差异通路，并利用GEO数据库验证CRC中FAK/Src/YAP轴的表达模式。构建氧化偶氮甲烷/葡聚糖硫酸钠（AOM/DSS）诱导的CRC小鼠模型，评估WMW对生存率、肿瘤负荷、结肠组织学变化及相关蛋白表达的影响。通过qRT-PCR检测下游基因CTGF和Axin2的表达，并在HCT116细胞模型中考察含WMW血清对FAK/Src/YAP信号通路的调控作用。最后，进行分子对接和分子动力学模拟。结果：UHPLC-HRMS/MS分析鉴定出WMW给药后15种循环成分。网络药理学分析显示，WMW相关靶点与CRC相关基因之间存在241个重叠靶点，这些靶点富集于炎症调控、细胞增殖和黏着斑相关通路，其中FAK/Src/YAP相关信号特征成为核心网络模块。在AOM/DSS诱导的CRC模型中，WMW治疗与体重、肿瘤负荷和结肠黏膜结构的变化相关，同时降低组织中VEGF和p53的表达水平。多组学分析显示，WMW干预后炎症、增殖和细胞外基质（ECM）重塑相关通路发生协调性改变。GEO数据集分析证实CRC组织中PTK2、Src和YAP1表达升高，支持临床CRC中黏着斑-YAP相关信号特征的异常。体内和体外实验表明，WMW干预与FAK、Src和YAP磷酸化水平降低、应力纤维形成减少、YAP核定位减弱以及CTGF和PCNA表达降低相关。分子对接和分子动力学模拟表明，多种循环成分能与FAK激酶结构域稳定相互作用，其中橙皮内酯表现出相对较优的结合特性。结论：这些发现表明，WMW干预与CRC中炎症相关信号、细胞增殖和细胞外基质重塑的协调性变化相关，其中黏着斑-YAP相关机械转导可能是一个潜在的相关特征。本研究提供了综合实验证据，支持进一步研究WMW及基于中药靶向黏着斑相关信号的CRC研究策略。
